candidate_rankings.selection_reason: Selected by lexicographic semantic, stability, confidence, complexity ranking.
Unselected: a higher-ranking exact stable bundle exists.
Unselected: frozen oracle mismatch or unstable repeats.

data.explanation: Independent authority-derived oracle distinguishes kit-interpreter defaults, runner.python conflicts, explicit consumer overrides, silence, topical mentions and out-of-scope ordinary Python scripts. Development separately tests assertions, checkable artifacts and future work.

criteria.no: No supporting artifact is cited, there is only a bare assertion/future intention, or no compliant delivered behavior is claimed.
criteria.unclear: A possible supporting reference appears, but its connection to the required default cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: A checkable path, diff, named test/result or command supports the claimed kit default under configured runner.python.

evidenced.instructions: Does item.text cite concrete checkable evidence supporting the claimed delivered ANC-022 default: helpers run on the kit venv despite runner.python when no explicit consumer helper override applies? A named passing test with that assertion, code path, diff or command output can support it; a bare assertion or future intention cannot.

criteria.no: No such content is stated, a different default is specified, or it is only deferred/future work. This includes ordinary Python-only changes expressly excluding helper execution; exclusion alone does not state the helper default.
criteria.unclear: The item affirmatively discusses helper interpreter selection but gives too little detail to determine its default or runner.python interaction. Do not use unclear for ordinary Python-only work that expressly excludes helper execution.
criteria.yes: The full kit-default obligation, including configured runner.python, is explicit as delivered behavior.

implemented.instructions: Does the delivered account in item.text state that the work implemented this complete obligation? By default sc_lint.* wheel helpers use the kit venv (.sc-lint/venv) interpreter even when [tool.sc-lint].runner.python is set. A separate explicit consumer helper override may change that default; runner.python alone is not that override. Future-only intent is not implementation. Judge the claim, independently of supporting evidence. Work limited to ordinary Python scripts and explicitly excluding helper execution does not state this helper-default obligation: answer no. An exclusion of helpers from a change is not a statement about their default interpreter.

criteria.no: The work concerns another activity, or expressly excludes helper execution.
criteria.unclear: The work description is too vague to identify whether helper execution is touched.
criteria.yes: Helper execution or its interpreter dispatch is touched, including refactoring it without interpreter details.

relevant.instructions: Does item.text describe work affecting how sc_lint.* wheel helper steps execute or choose their interpreter? Judge only scope overlap. An explicit exclusion of helper execution means ordinary Python-step changes alone are outside this scope.

criteria.no: No incompatible behavior is stated; silence, vague topic mentions, and a separate explicit override preserving the default are not conflict.
criteria.unclear: The text describes a possible incompatible rule but its actual default versus explicit-override behavior is ambiguous.
criteria.yes: The text explicitly replaces the helper kit default with runner.python or another default, or otherwise rules out the required default.

violated.instructions: Does item.text specify behavior incompatible with this default? By default sc_lint.* wheel helpers use the kit venv (.sc-lint/venv) interpreter even when [tool.sc-lint].runner.python is set. A separate explicit consumer helper override may change that default; runner.python alone is not that override. Judge conflict alone: silence and unspecified implementation details are not conflict.
